title_en: Hua Zhixi et al. v. Hua Ningxi et al. — estate inheritance dispute
keywords_en: Civil; Inheritance dispute; First instance; Intermediate people's court; Beijing; Shanghai; Natural person; Legal person; Marriage Law; Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation); Validity of family agreement; Determination of foster relationship; Definition of estate scope; Inheritance by subrogation; Partial support; Inheritance; Family agreement; Foster relationship; Foreign-related inheritance; Divorce
full_text_en:
Hua Zhixi et al. v. Hua Ningxi et al. — Inheritance Dispute

Plaintiff: Hua Zhixi, male, 38 years old, worker at Shanghai Optical Machinery Factory, residing at No. 41, Lane 1857, Huaihai Middle Road, Shanghai.

Plaintiff: Hua Chunxi, male, 41 years old, worker at Shanghai No. 3 Pharmaceutical Factory, same address as above.

Plaintiff: Hua Qiangzhen, female, 42 years old, engineer at the Inspection Department of Beijing No. 2 Machine Tool Factory, residing at No. 12, Lane 4, Gongmenkou, Fuchengmennei, Beijing.

Defendant: Hua Wanzhen (also agent ad litem for Li Jieshou), female, 63 years old, residing at Room 304, Building 22, Dormitory of the Design Institute, Ministry of Textile Industry, Beijing.

Defendant: Hua Ningxi (also agent ad litem for Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng), male, 58 years old, Chief Engineer at the Paper Research Institute, Ministry of Light Industry, residing at No. 139, Zhugan Hutong, Chaoyangmennei, Beijing.

Defendant: Li Jieshou (wife of Hua Chunxi), female, 60 years old, American citizen, currently residing in the United States.

Defendant: Hua Kezeng (eldest daughter of Hua Chunxi), female, 28 years old, American citizen, currently residing in the United States.

Defendant: Hua Anzeng (second daughter of Hua Chunxi), female, 27 years old, American citizen, currently residing in the United States.

Defendant: Hua Dezeng (youngest daughter of Hua Chunxi), female, 21 years old, American citizen, currently residing in the United States.

Third Party: Xu Pingqian, female, 65 years old, residing at No. 41, Lane 1857, Huaihai Middle Road, Shanghai.

The decedent Hua Dongchen married Li Yurong and Xu Pingqian successively before the liberation. Li Yurong gave birth to three children: daughter Hua Wanzhen, sons Hua Ningxi and Hua Chunxi (Hua Chunxi went to the United States in his early years, died of illness in 1969, leaving behind his wife Li Jieshou and daughters Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng). Xu Pingqian gave birth to three children: daughter Hua Qiangzhen, sons Hua Chunxi and Hua Zhixi. In July 1959, Hua Dongchen and Xu Pingqian divorced by agreement, and the three children born to Xu Pingqian were placed in the custody of Hua Dongchen. From then on, Hua Qiangzhen, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Zhixi were raised by Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong, living together in Shanghai. In 1962, Hua Dongchen fell ill, and Xu Pingqian returned to care for him. In 1963, Hua Dongchen died of illness. On October 18, 1964, under the auspices of Li Yurong, a family agreement was reached among Hua Wanzhen, Hua Ningxi, Hua Qiangzhen, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Zhixi: all of Hua Dongchen's property was to be inherited by Li Yurong, who would pay Hua Qiangzhen a subsidy of RMB 5,000, and pay Hua Chunxi and Hua Zhixi each a maintenance fee of RMB 11,400. Li Yurong's maintenance obligations toward them would then cease, and there would be no further economic relationship. In 1969, Li Yurong moved to Beijing to live with her son Hua Ningxi, and died of illness in 1971. Subsequently, Hua Zhixi, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Qiangzhen filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, requesting a fair distribution of the estates of their father Hua Dongchen and mother Li Yurong. The defendants Hua Ningxi and Hua Wanzhen argued that Hua Dongchen's estate had already been distributed under the family agreement of 1964 and objected to a new distribution; they also asserted that the plaintiffs Hua Zhixi, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Qiangzhen had no right to inherit Li Yurong's estate. The defendants Li Jieshou and Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng respectively appointed Hua Wanzhen and Hua Ningxi as their agents ad litem to participate in the proceedings, requesting the people's court to protect their rights and interests in accordance with the law.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court accepted the case pursuant to Article 17(1) and Article 30(4) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation). Upon trial, the following facts were found: The estates registered in the names of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong included multiple stock dividends and bank deposits totaling RMB 254,256.19; a building at No. 41, Lane 1857, Huaihai Middle Road, Shanghai, valued at RMB 37,028.71. When the policies were implemented in 1979, Hua Zhixi and Hua Chunxi withdrew deposits and interest in the name of Hua Dongchen totaling RMB 26,362.87, and Hua Wanzhen and Hua Ningxi withdrew deposits and interest in the name of Li Yurong totaling RMB 15,318.85, which should also be included in the estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong. The total verified estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong amounted to RMB 332,966.62. Furthermore, Xu Pingqian, in 1979 claiming to be Hua Dongchen's second wife, withdrew the converted value of property confiscated during the "Cultural Revolution" of RMB 74,972.29, and the building at No. 136, Zhugan Hutong, Chaoyangmennei, Beijing, in the name of Hua Ningxi, whether these should be included in the estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong remains disputed among the parties. Since the outcome of this case has a legal interest relationship with Xu Pingqian, in accordance with Article 48(2) of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), Xu Pingqian was added as a third party to participate in the proceedings. To ensure smooth enforcement of the judgment, in accordance with Article 92(1) of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), preservative measures were taken to freeze the above movable property.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court found in its adjudication: At the time of the divorce between Hua Dongchen and Xu Pingqian, the plaintiffs Hua Zhixi, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Qiangzhen were all minors and were jointly raised by Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong, thus forming a relationship of support and dependency between Li Yurong and them. Therefore, the three children born to Li Yurong and the three children born to Xu Pingqian all have the right to inherit the estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong. Regarding the family agreement of 1964, since Hua Zhixi was still a minor at that time and lacked full legal capacity, his right of inheritance should have been exercised by his statutory agent Li Yurong. Li Yurong, as Hua Zhixi's statutory agent, should have protected his lawful rights and interests, but the agreement she presided over clearly infringed upon the lawful inheritance rights of the principal. Furthermore, Hua Chunxi did not participate in the negotiation of the agreement, so the agreement should be deemed invalid. The respective estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong should be fairly distributed among the six children in accordance with the law. Since Hua Chunxi died in 1969, his share of Hua Dongchen's estate should be transferred to his lawful heirs, namely his wife Li Jieshou and daughters Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng, to be inherited jointly. Additionally, because Hua Chunxi predeceased Li Yurong, his share of Li Yurong's estate should be inherited by his daughters Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng by way of subrogation. The converted value of the confiscated property of RMB 74,972.29, withdrawn by Xu Pingqian in 1979 under the name of Hua Dongchen's second wife, was verified through examination of relevant archival materials from the relevant units. This sum represented the converted value of property confiscated in the name of Hua Dongchen from the building at No. 41, Lane 1857, Huaihai Middle Road, Shanghai, and from safe deposit boxes in banks. At the time of confiscation, Xu Pingqian was residing in the building, and some of the confiscated items were her personal property. However, since Li Yurong had passed away, the confiscated property could no longer be clearly distinguished. Additionally, considering that Xu Pingqian had cared for Hua Dongchen when he was bedridden due to illness, a portion of Hua Dongchen's estate should be appropriately allocated to her. Under these circumstances, RMB 40,000 is extracted from this sum as belonging to Xu Pingqian, and the remaining RMB 34,972.29 is included in the estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong, to be jointly inherited by the six children. The property at No. 139, Zhugan Hutong, Chaoyangmennei, Beijing, is registered in the name of Hua Ningxi. The claim by Hua Zhixi et al. that this house is parental property lacks sufficient evidence and is not recognized. The building at No. 41, Lane 1857, Huaihai Middle Road, Shanghai, is part of the estates of Hua Dongchen and Li Yurong. Hua Zhixi, Hua Chunxi, and others have continuously resided in the building. For ease of living and use, the building should be valued and distributed.

Accordingly, on January 29, 1985, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 18(2) of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that parents and children have the right to inherit each other's property, and on the basis of equal distribution among the heirs, but taking into consideration the different degrees of support provided to the decedents by the plaintiffs and defendants, rendered the following judgment:

1. Hua Wanzhen and Hua Ningxi each receive RMB 60,303.40; Hua Qiangzhen, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Zhixi each receive RMB 50,000; Li Jieshou, Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng jointly receive RMB 60,303.40.

2. The building at No. 41, Lane 1857, Huaihai Middle Road, Shanghai, which has been continuously occupied by Hua Zhixi and Hua Chunxi, shall, for convenience of living and use, be owned jointly by Hua Qiangzhen, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Zhixi. The building is valued at RMB 37,028.71. Hua Qiangzhen, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Zhixi shall each pay RMB 6,171.45 to Hua Wanzhen and Hua Ningxi as the converted value of the building, and shall pay a total of RMB 6,171.45 to Li Jieshou, Hua Kezeng, Hua Anzeng, and Hua Dezeng as the converted value of the building. The costs of property valuation and real estate taxes shall be borne by Hua Qiangzhen, Hua Chunxi, and Hua Zhixi.

3. The property at No. 139, Zhugan Hutong, Chaoyangmennei, Beijing, is confirmed as owned by Hua Ningxi.

4. Xu Pingqian shall receive RMB 40,000.

At its 237th session on November 29, 1985, the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 11(1) of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, and in summarizing judicial experience, held that in adjudicating this case, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court lawfully confirmed the relationship of support and dependency formed between the plaintiffs and the decedent, upheld their lawful inheritance rights, invalidated the void family agreement, protected the litigation rights of the Chinese-American parties in this case, and safeguarded their lawful rights and interests. This case serves as a reference for people's courts at all levels.
